## Dummy Server Data

### Description
For instances when there is no server setup yet but you have an idea what kind of data will be sent by it you can use the `dummyMessage` and `dummySettings` properties of the GameModel and GameSettings classes respectively.

:warning: For this data to be used the engineName must be set to `'unknown'` in the game config.

### Basic Usage
This will still send a request to the server using the spin endpoint to retain error behaviour for things like TimeKeeper as well as getting valid PlayerData. However the GameMessage and GameSettings objects it returns will be ignored and replaced with the dummy data set as in the examples below.

To simulate a **NewPlayer response** do not define a `dummyMessage`.

#### Examples
```ts
// Example GameModel with dummyMessage data
class GameModel implements IBaseGameModel {
    // ... other properties ommited for example simplicity

    // IGameMessageResponse should extend IBaseMessageResponse
    public dummyMessage: IGameMessageResponse = {
        GameComplete: false,
        Stake: 5
    };

    public setData(responseData: IBaseServerResponse): void {
        // ... implementation ommited for example simplicity
    }
}
```
```ts
// Example GameSettings with dummySettings data
class GameSettings implements IBaseGameSettingsModel {
    // ... other properties ommited for example simplicity

    // IGameSettingsResponse should extend IBaseSettingsResponse
    public dummySettings: IGameSettingsResponse = {
        DefaultStake: 5,
        Version: 'dummy',
        StakeOptions: [5, 10, 20, 50, 100]
    };

    public setData(responseData: IBaseServerResponse): void {
        // ... implementation ommited for example simplicity
    }
}
```
